summary: Owned units s0045–s0066 are the close of Wang Xizhi's letter to Yin Hao and the opening of his letter to the Prince of Kuaiji. They name no births, deaths, ages, or 同生 twins. Chen Sheng and Wu Guang are only a present-tense 勝廣 fear in the Hao letter and are correctly kept as retrospective reception with empty active hints. Yao and Shun appear only as 古人…堯舜 exemplars; legendary antiquity is the right qualitative placement and is not a Jin life date. The defective row is the closed AD 353–354 window on the Kuaiji letter (claim-173, claim-186, claim-210 and the p021/p024 hints). The Chinese gives 又與會稽王箋 and deictic 今, not a regnal year. One chapter-and-annals reading places that 箋 after the post-山桑 Hao letter, hence conventional 永和九年–十年 / AD 353–354 (Hao dismissed 永和十年二月). A competing chronology dates 《上會稽王笺》 to 永和八年 / AD 352, after the 許昌 setback while Hao still planned to go on, and the letter's 可欣之會 plus the named forward posts fit that earlier moment. A 353–354 interval chooses one reading and invents two exclusive endpoints. Conventional 永和八年–十年 labels correspond to AD 352–354 and need not equal the Gregorian year of every lunar month. Wang Xizhi's hint AD 353–355 then adds a further unsupported 355 endpoint: supplied context dates only the 永和九年 Lanting gathering, and 355 is the later resignation, not this letter. Academia Sinica's converter defaults to Julian before 1582; these claims are year-only conventional labels, not month-day Gregorian event dates.

itemChecks.event: The Prince of Kuaiji is the named addressee of Wang Xizhi's letter arguing that Yin Hao must not campaign north.
itemChecks.reason: The dated event is the Prince's role as addressee of 又與會稽王箋陳浩不宜北伐, not a campaign or accession of his own. s0058 supplies no ruler, reign, or year. The input start AD 353 follows only the reading that this 箋 is contemporary with the Hao letter written after 姚襄所敗 (annals: 永和九年十月 山桑; conventional AD 353). The input end AD 354 follows Hao's dismissal in 永和十年二月, after which advice that Hao must not campaign is moot. A competing witness dates 《上會稽王笺》 to 永和八年 / AD 352, after the 許昌/誡橋 setback while Hao still planned to continue; 今雖有可欣之會 and the named posts 許昌、譙郡、梁、彭城 fit that earlier moment. Conventional 永和八年–十年 = AD 352–354 as year labels, and a reign year need not equal the Gregorian year of every month (永和八年十二月 already reaches AD 353). The closed 353–354 interval therefore drops a supported 352 reading and treats both endpoints as known. Owner of the writing is Wang Xizhi; the Prince is only the recipient.

findings.problem: The Kuaiji letter is dated with a closed AD 353–354 interval although the Chinese has only 又與會稽王箋 and deictic 今. That interval keeps the post-山桑 / 永和九年–十年 reading and drops the competing 永和八年 / AD 352 dating of 《上會稽王笺》, so both endpoints are over-precise for a yearless 箋.
findings.action: Revise claim-173, claim-186, and claim-210 to a conventional AD 352–354 uncertainty window (永和八年–十年 of 晉穆帝) that preserves both the 352 chronology of the 笺 and the post-山桑 353–354 narrative reading; keep sourceDate as the Chinese 又與會稽王箋 / 今; state that these are reign-year labels, not a month-day Gregorian date. Synchronize hints-p021 and hints-p024 to the same window. Do not pick a single winning year and do not leave a one-sided bound that excludes 352.

findings.problem: Wang Xizhi's active hint AD 353–355 extends past every supplied personal event (contested Kuaiji letter; explicit 永和九年 Lanting; undated famine). The 355 end is the later resignation, not this letter cluster, and claim-210's exclusive 353–354 stamp also fails to preserve the 352 reading of the 箋.
findings.action: After repairing the Kuaiji-letter window, reset hints-p028 to the supported personal events only: the repaired letter uncertainty plus the explicit 永和九年 / AD 353 Lanting gathering.
